hero.h1: Gas Line Repair in Algonquin, IL
hero.sub: A gas smell near the furnace, a red tag from the utility or an old connector behind the range. Our licensed plumbers find gas leaks, repair the piping and pressure-test it before we leave. From our office on Esplanade Drive.

blocks.h2: Do You Smell Gas? Act Now

steps.body: Don't stop to open windows or grab things.
Switches, phones and garage door openers can spark.
Nicor Gas or 911, from the street.
We'll find and repair the leak.

blocks.h2: Signs Your Gas Line Needs Attention

tiles.body: Water heater, furnace, range or dryer.

tiles.h3: A Red Tag From the Utility
tiles.body: Service stays off until the piping is repaired and tested.
Outdoor kitchens and fire pits strain older layouts.
Underground lines can leak out of sight.

bodies: If you suspect a small leak or the utility shut off service, we find the source with electronic detectors and soap tests, then pressure-test the system to confirm it's sealed.
In newer homes, most leaks are at appliance connectors, flexible lines and fittings added after construction. Once repaired, we test the whole system so service can be restored.

blocks.intro: More than half of Algonquin homes were built between 1990 and 2009, and many gas systems have been added to.

items.body: Patio gas lines are popular here. A buried line that wasn't installed right can leak.
Many 1990s and 2000s homes use flexible gas tubing in places. It needs proper bonding and protection.
Old connectors from the original range or dryer should be replaced when the appliance is.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: Gas work done right, then tested.

steps.body: Gas line work should be done by a licensed pro. Ours are licensed and trained for it.
We find it, then quote it.
Before the gas comes back on.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
items.preview: Leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
items.answer: Leave right away without touching switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside. Then call us for the repair.

items.q: Can you test my outdoor gas line?
items.answer: Yes. We pressure-test buried lines to grills, fire pits and pool heaters and find leaks if there are any.

items.q: What is flexible gas tubing, and is it safe?
items.preview: It's safe when installed and bonded correctly.
items.answer: Corrugated stainless steel tubing is common in newer homes. It's safe when it's installed, protected and bonded correctly. We can check yours.

items.q: Who fixes the gas line, the utility or a plumber?
items.preview: The utility up to the meter, a licensed plumber after it.
items.answer: Nicor Gas handles the line up to and including the meter. Everything after it is the homeowner's and should be repaired by a licensed plumber.

items.q: What does gas line repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the leak and the line. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on where the leak is and how much pipe needs work. We quote a flat rate before we start.
